record.title: Datang’s Zhongwei compute campus solar phase is reported operational; wind supply remains unverified
record.summary: A report hosted by the National Energy Administration’s Northwest Office says China Datang’s 500-MW photovoltaic plant for the Zhongwei Cloud Base entered operation on 2026-05-02. It describes a dedicated-line physical-supply arrangement for incremental data-center load and bilateral power-market transactions for existing load. The article says the separate 1.5-GW wind phase was planned for full grid connection in September 2026 and that 2.29 TWh per year could meet campus demand after the first phase is fully operational. These are attributed project reports; this review did not establish post-September wind commissioning, metered generation, campus delivery or realized cost and reliability effects.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A National Energy Administration Northwest Office report published 2026-05-06 says China Datang's 500-MW Zhongwei Cloud Base photovoltaic plant entered operation on 2026-05-02.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The report describes a dedicated-line physical-supply arrangement for incremental data-center load and bilateral power-market transactions for existing load; it says 1.5-GW wind capacity was planned for full grid connection in September 2026, with 2.29 TWh per year expected after the first phase is fully operational.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reviewed sources do not establish full wind-phase commissioning, sustained or interval-measured generation, delivery matched to campus load, cost, reliability, emissions, or quality-qualified compute output.

evidence_gaps.description: Post-September commissioning status for the planned 1.5-GW wind phase is unknown.
No interval generation, campus delivery, storage dispatch, curtailment or grid-exchange records were examined.
Realized electricity price, reliability, emissions and cost per useful compute remain unmeasured.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported 500-MW direct-supply solar phase is operating as described, it is a meaningful local milestone for power procurement and infrastructure planning at a large compute campus. The score reflects the potential relevance of the physical supply arrangement, not verified generation, campus delivery, cost, reliability or useful compute impact.
limitations: The accessible article is hosted by the NEA Northwest Office but attributes its source to China News Network; it is not an operator meter record or independent audit.
The report says the 500-MW PV phase entered operation but provides no interval generation or campus-load matching data.
The 1.5-GW wind full-connection date was a plan for September 2026; post-deadline status was not established in this review.
The 2.29 TWh/year figure is conditional on first-phase completion and is not measured current generation or campus delivery.
No delivered-power price, reliability, curtailment, emissions intensity or useful-compute denominator was reviewed.

relationships.summary: Distinct project milestone: the related record covers first turbines in the separate Chang Le wind segment; this record covers the earlier 500-MW PV phase.

The article says the separate 1.5-GW wind phase was planned for full grid connection in September 2026 and that 2.29 TWh per year could meet campus demand after the first phase is fully operational. technical.claimed_result: The NEA-hosted report says the 500-MW PV phase entered operation on May 2, 2026. It describes physical supply for incremental load and bilateral trading for existing load; no generation or delivery series is included.
technical.demonstrated_result: The report publication and its attributed commissioning account are directly inspectable. Actual metered generation, campus receipt and wind-phase completion are not established here.
technical.mechanism: The reported design uses a dedicated transmission line for physical PV supply to incremental data-center load, while existing load relies on bilateral electricity-market transactions; the report describes wind as a planned complement during PV downtime.
technical.regime: One 500-MW photovoltaic phase at the Zhongwei Cloud Base reported operational on 2026-05-02; a separate 1.5-GW wind phase was planned for full grid connection in September 2026. The 2.29 TWh/year figure is conditional on first-phase completion.
technical.reproducibility: The report is publicly accessible, but the commissioning and supply claims were not independently audited or reproduced from meter records.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched electricity-supply or operating-cost baseline is reported or inspected.

brief.title: Datang’s Zhongwei compute campus solar phase is reported operational; wind supply remains unverified
brief.why_it_matters: Large compute campuses increasingly need substantial, reliable electricity. A reported 500-MW solar phase with a dedicated-line supply design is a meaningful infrastructure milestone to track alongside the separate wind project. Nameplate capacity and commissioning reports do not show energy delivered to the campus, cost, reliability, or compute output, so the economic effect remains unknown.

other.title: First 14 turbines in Datang Zhongwei's Chang Le wind project connect and generate
other.summary: China Energy Engineering Corporation reports that on 2026-10-05 the first 14 turbines in the first section of Datang Zhongwei's Chang Le 500-MW wind project completed energization and grid connection and generated successfully. The builder says 75 turbines are planned for the segment and links it to the Zhongwei compute campus. This is a partial commissioning milestone; the report provides no interval generation or campus-delivery data.
